title: Privileged admin SSO gap analysis and threat playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket captures a cross-functional action plan following the recent pen-test and security review focused on RBAC v2, audit logging gaps, and SSO/SAML admin flows. Objective: produce a prioritized mitigation plan, update the threat model, and ship a small playbook + tactical fixes for the admin surface (console/API/SAML assertions/privileged token lifecycle). Outputs: threat-playbook.md, mitigation PRs, updated threat-model diagram, test cases, and an incident runbook for privilege escalation / SAML replay scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Threat model updated to include RBAC v2 role inheritance and admin delegation patterns
Concrete mitigations implemented for top 3 pen-test findings with PRs and tests
Audit logging emits immutable, signed events for admin-critical actions and retention policy configured
SSO/SAML flow hardening: assertion replay protection, short-lived admin sessions, required MFA enforcement
Console surfaces 'admin action' warnings and records actor/justification for break-glass events
Playbook documented and reviewed by Security, PM, and Design; tabletop run completed
decisions: Adopt role-based separation: remove global 'super-admin' single toggle; instead ship 'org-admin' + scoped 'service-admin' roles
Require MFA for any account granted an admin role via SSO; enforce at identity provider and validate session claims in runtime
Audit events for admin actions will be written to an append-only, signed stream (log signing using KMS key per-region)
Short-term mitigation: enable strict session TTL for SAML admin assertions (default 15 minutes) and rotate binding certificates quarterly
Long-term: implement fine-grained admin delegation model and RBAC auditing UI in Console release 2026.06
